liveAnswer: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) is a data-forwarding technology that uses labels to route packets instead of relying on IP addresses. Routers (label-switching routers) swap labels at each hop, enabling faster forwarding, traffic engineering, and VPN services. Common use cases include MPLS VPNs, QoS enforcement, and path optimization across service-provider networks.
